cues.en: I don't know about you, but I find cooking rice to be an extremely difficult task.
cues.zh: 我不知道你们怎么想，但我总觉得煮饭是件极其困难的事。

cues.en: Luckily, somebody invented the automatic rice cooker and now all my rice cooking problems have been solved. Hooray.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，有人发明了自动电饭煲，现在我所有的煮饭难题都迎刃而解了。太棒了。

cues.en: Now you might think that rice cookers are a pretty boring small kitchen appliance, but actually, they're among the... Well, okay. If we're looking at what they do, then yeah. This ain't no toaster, that's for sure. But while the device itself may seem pretty unremarkable,
cues.zh: 你可能觉得电饭煲不过是个挺无聊的厨房小家电，但实际上，它们……好吧。如果只看功能，确实如此。肯定比不上烤面包机那么好玩。不过，虽然这机器本身看似平平无奇，

cues.en: and indeed is, the principle by which it works is fascinating.
cues.zh: 而且确实很普通，但它的工作原理却相当精妙。

cues.en: Simply by exploiting one of the chemical properties of water, this device can tell when the rice has been cooked, and the result is a perfectly cooked batch of the world's second favorite grain.
cues.zh: 仅仅利用水的一项物理化学特性，它就能判断米饭何时煮好，做出一锅口感完美的米饭——这可是全世界第二受欢迎的主食。

cues.en: Assuming you got the water to rice ratio correct, that is. So how does it work? Well, to find out, first we need to learn a little bit about water.
cues.zh: 当然，前提是你水和米的比例没放错。那么它是怎么工作的呢？要想搞清楚，我们首先得了解一点关于水的知识。

cues.en: As I'm sure we all know, at sea level, water boils at 212 degrees Fahrenheit. Isn't that just a delightfully easy number to remember? I don't know what the heck that is in Celsius, probably some silly arbitrary thing. But anyway, that number isn't the whole story. You see, water doesn't just boil at that temperature, it starts to boil. See, if you've got a pot of water on the stove and you watch its temperature rise with a thermometer,
cues.zh: 大家都知道，在标准大气压下，水的沸点是华氏 212 度。这个数字是不是特别好记？我反正不知道换成摄氏度是多少，估计是某种随意规定的数字吧。但不管怎样，这个数字并不是故事的全部。你看，水不仅在这个温度沸腾，而且是开始沸腾。如果在炉子上放一锅水，用温度计观察水温上升，

cues.en: well, what do you suppose happens once it gets to boiling point? You can see the temperature steadily rising as it approaches,
cues.zh: 你猜猜一旦达到沸点会发生什么？随着接近沸点，你可以看到温度稳步上升，

cues.en: so you might think that once it hits boiling point the water will just poof disappear and turn into a big old cloud of water vapor.
cues.zh: 你可能会以为，一旦达到沸点，水就会“噗”的一声彻底消失，变成一大团水蒸气。

cues.en: But of course, that's not what happens. The temperature just plateaus,
cues.zh: 但事实显然并非如此。温度只会维持在平台期，

cues.en: and it won't go any higher. But the stove or hot plate is still dumping energy into the water, so why isn't it getting any hotter?
cues.zh: 不会再继续升高了。可炉灶或加热盘还在源源不断地向水注入能量，那水温为什么不继续上升呢？

cues.en: The answer is physics, and more specifically,
cues.zh: 答案就在物理学中，更具体地说，

cues.en: the principle known as the latent heat of vaporization.
cues.zh: 在于被称为“汽化潜热”的物理原理。

cues.en: This is a fun concept important to many fields of study, from meteorology to refrigeration.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的概念，在从气象学到制冷技术的众多领域中都至关重要。

cues.en: Also known as enthalpy of vaporization,
cues.zh: 它也被称为汽化焓，

cues.en: this is the amount of energy required to transition a liquid into a gas.
cues.zh: 指的是将液体转化为气体所需要的能量。

cues.en: And it's a lot more energy than just raising the temperature of that liquid. Okay so what we need to understand here is how latent heat differs from sensible heat. Sensible heat is something like, oh I don't know, 68 degrees? That's a pretty sensible room temperature. Oh.
cues.zh: 这可比单纯升高液体温度所需的能量要多得多。好了，这里我们需要搞清楚的是潜热与显热的区别。显热就像……呃，比如 68 度？那是个很合情理（sensible）的室温。噢。

cues.en: Sensible,
cues.zh: 可感知的（Sensible），

cues.en: like can be sensed. Got it. Sensible heat is the figure we can sense, or measure. The thermometer is looking at sensible heat when it tells us how hot something is. But as the water, or any other substance, reaches its phase change temperature,
cues.zh: 也就是“能够被感知到”。懂了。显热就是我们可以感知或测量的数值。温度计告诉我们物体有多热时，反映的就是显热。但当水或任何其他物质达到相变温度时，

cues.en: adding energy into it will not raise the sensible heat.
cues.zh: 继续向其中注入能量并不会提高显热。

cues.en: Instead, that energy gets absorbed by the molecules to free them from their liquid state, and that takes a heck of a lot of energy. We don't need to be too worried about that extra energy right now. We'll get to that when we tackle air conditioning and refrigeration.
cues.zh: 相反，这些能量被分子吸收，使它们摆脱液态，而这需要大量能量。我们现在不必太担心这部分额外能量。等讲到空调和制冷时再处理。

cues.en: But what you need to know for the purposes of cooking rice is that liquid water cannot exist at a temperature higher than its boiling point. Dumping more energy into it will simply make it boil away faster.
cues.zh: 但就煮米饭而言，你需要知道：液态水不可能存在于高于其沸点的温度。继续给它加能量，只会让它更快地沸腾蒸发掉。

cues.en: It will not make it get any hotter.
cues.zh: 并不会让它变得更热。

cues.en: So what does that have to do with cooking rice? Well, see, cooking rice is all about making water hot so that the rice will absorb it and the starch just converts up to the other things and all that jazz.
cues.zh: 那这和煮米饭有什么关系？你看，煮米饭就是把水加热，让米吸收水，淀粉转化成别的东西，诸如此类。

cues.en: And that rice is cooked once it has absorbed all the water. You don't want to keep cooking it after that point or it will burn, and you don't want to not cook it long enough or you'll have rice al dente which I'm pretty sure isn't actually a thing. So in an ideal world, we'd have a way to tell precisely when that rice has finished cooking.
cues.zh: 米吸收完所有水后就熟了。之后继续煮会烧焦，煮得不够久又会得到所谓 al dente 的米饭——我很确定这其实不算回事。所以理想情况下，我们得有办法精确判断米饭何时煮好。

cues.en: And thanks to latent heat of vaporization,
cues.zh: 而多亏了汽化潜热，

cues.en: we do.
cues.zh: 我们确实有办法。

cues.en: See, water can't get hotter than its boiling point. But cooked rice can.
cues.zh: 你看，水不能热过沸点，但煮熟的米饭可以。

cues.en: And once you know that little factoid, you can easily make a device which will cook rice to completion and automatically stop.
cues.zh: 一旦知道这个小知识，你就能轻松做出一个把饭煮到熟、然后自动停止的装置。

cues.en: This is a very basic rice cooker. It cooks rice,
cues.zh: 这是一个非常基础的电饭锅。它会煮饭，

cues.en: and that's it. None of that fancy multifunction
cues.zh: 就这样。没有那些花哨的多功能

cues.en: nonsense.
cues.zh: 乱七八糟的玩意儿。

cues.en: Side note, I actually have a nicer rice cooker with a whole electronic interface thing that can do fancy things like slow cook or steam vegetables,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我其实有个更好的电饭锅，带整套电子界面，能做慢炖或蒸菜之类的花哨功能，

cues.en: but it's got one of those gasket deals going on in the lid, and frankly it gets really gross all the time, and it's a pain to clean.
cues.zh: 但它的盖子有那种密封圈结构，说实话总是变得很恶心，而且清洗很麻烦。

cues.en: Now I'm not certainly someone who eats rice as a staple food, but when I discovered that this cheap basic unit had just plain glass lid and both it and the bowl are dishwasher safe, I was like life changer and bought it on the spot.
cues.zh: 我并不是把米饭当主食的人，但当我发现这个便宜的基础款只有普通玻璃盖，而且盖子和内胆都能用洗碗机洗时，我心想“改变生活”，当场就买了。

cues.en: Truthfully, I prefer it to my fancier one by a large margin simply because it doesn't get gross and it cooks rice just as well, which is all I use a rice cooker for anyway. Plus, it doesn't beep incessantly for fifteen seconds when it's done, so that's a nice plus. Sometimes basic is in fact better, but that's all down to your personal priorities and preferences.
cues.zh: 说实话，我远比那个花哨的更喜欢它，因为它不会变恶心，煮饭也一样好——反正我用饭锅就只为煮饭。另外，煮好后它不会没完没了地滴滴叫十五秒，这是个不错的加分项。有时候基础款确实更好，但这全看你的个人优先级和偏好。

cues.en: And I'm sure you all will tell me why my priorities and preferences are wrong.
cues.zh: 我肯定你们都会告诉我，我的优先级和偏好错在哪。

cues.en: Anyway, this device is so incredibly simple and yet entirely automatic and I just love that sort of thing. At the bottom, you've got a round heating element with a little button thing poking up through the center. This guy is spring loaded and is the heart of its automatic operation.
cues.zh: 总之，这个装置简单得不可思议，却完全自动，我就喜欢这种东西。底部有一个圆形加热元件，中间伸出一个按钮似的小东西。这个部件带弹簧，是它自动运行的核心。

cues.en: The rice cooker has two modes, cooking and keep warm. Whenever it's plugged in, it's in the warming mode.
cues.zh: 这款电饭煲有两种模式：煮饭和保温。只要插上电源，它就处于保温模式。

cues.en: If we flip it over and take off the bottom, we'll see that there's a bunch of wires. In the keep warm state, current comes in through the power cord and passes through this big resistor to limit the current before going through the heating element.
cues.zh: 把它翻过来拆开底盖，就能看到一堆电线。在保温状态下，电流从电源线进来，经过这个大电阻限流后，再流经加热元件。

cues.en: The lever to engage cooking is attached to that button thing, and importantly it closes these contacts.
cues.zh: 用来启动煮饭的杠杆连着那个按钮部件，关键是它会闭合这组触点。

cues.en: This bypasses the resistor and allows the heating element to run at full power.
cues.zh: 这样就绕过了电阻，让发热元件能够全功率运行。

cues.en: In this case it's a mere 300 watts. This is after all a tiny little rice cooker. Also, this changes which of the little neon indicators lights up. Useful.
cues.zh: 在这里只有区区 300 瓦，毕竟这只是个袖珍小电饭煲。另外，这还会切换点亮哪颗霓虹指示灯。挺实用的。

cues.en: You'll see that right now I cannot get the lever to stay engaged. That's because the button thing isn't depressed. This serves as a safety feature to prevent the heating element from operating at full power if the pot were to be removed.
cues.zh: 你会发现现在我没法让杠杆固定住。这是因为那个按钮还没按下去。这是一种安全机制，防止内胆拿走时发热元件全功率运行。

cues.en: Ordinarily, the weight of the bowl would press down on it, but in this case I need to substitute my fingers.
cues.zh: 平时内胆自身的重量会把它压下去，但这里我得用手指按着。

cues.en: With it depressed, you'll see that the lever will now stick in the down position.
cues.zh: 按下去之后，你会看到杠杆现在就能卡在下方位置了。

cues.en: What's keeping it there is a permanent magnet, which you can just barely see here. And this is where things get really interesting. The magnet is sticking to the bottom of the button, and it's overcoming the force of a second spring inside the button trying to push it away. Which luckily it manages to do. But here's the thing about magnets.
cues.zh: 把它吸在那里的是块永磁铁，在这里隐约能看到。真正有意思的地方来了：磁铁吸在按钮底部，克服了按钮内部第二个弹簧向外推的弹力。幸运的是它成功吸住了。不过关于磁铁，有这么一回事。

cues.en: Get things hot, and suddenly magnets don't work anymore.
cues.zh: 温度一升高，磁铁突然就不管用了。

cues.en: Uh-oh. Here comes a blanket statement abatement alert. Magnets are confusing.
cues.zh: 哎呀，这里先插播一条防杠免责声明：磁学真的很让人头大。

cues.en: Ferromagnetism,
cues.zh: 铁磁性、

cues.en: paramagnetism,
cues.zh: 顺磁性、

cues.en: curie points. There's just so much that hurts my brain. So, please do not assume I'm an expert here because I am not. Regarding this magnetic phenomenon I'm about to describe,
cues.zh: 居里点。实在有太多让人烧脑的概念了。所以大家千万别把我当专家，我真不是。关于我接下来要说的这种磁现象，

cues.en: this is my very best interpretation from what I've uncovered through looking at patents, a very rudimentary understanding of magnetic interaction, and also some forum threads where people were arguing about this. If I've gotten something wrong here, please correct me in the comments. And also, please check to see if someone else has already provided a correction, thanks. All magnetic materials have what's called a Curie temperature, or Curie point. For ordinary ferromagnetic
cues.zh: 这是我查阅专利、凭借对磁相互作用的粗浅理解，以及看了论坛里各路神仙争论后，所能做出的最好解释。如果我有说错的地方，欢迎在评论区指正。但也请先看一眼是不是已经有人提过了，谢谢。所有磁性材料都有所谓的居里温度，或者叫居里点。对于普通的铁磁性

cues.en: materials, once you reach this temperature they cease to be ferromagnetic at all. In the case of a permanent magnet, if you get it to the Curie temperature,
cues.zh: 材料，一旦达到这个温度，就会彻底失去铁磁性。如果是永磁铁，要是加热到了居里温度，

cues.en: you've broken the magnet permanently.
cues.zh: 你就彻底把它给废了。

cues.en: So now it's a permanent not magnet.
cues.zh: 于是它就成了一块“永久不磁铁”。

cues.en: But materials that are attracted to permanent magnets will regain their attraction once they've cooled back down. This button thing is made of an alloy that has a Curie temperature just a bit higher than the boiling point of water.
cues.zh: 但能被永磁体吸引的材料，一旦冷却下来就会恢复磁性。这个类似按钮的小部件是由一种合金制成的，其居里温度刚好比水的沸点稍高一点。

cues.en: This allows it to function as a temperature dependent kill switch. Thanks to the outer spring, it's always held firmly in contact with the bottom of the pot, which ensures it and the pot are at nearly equal temperatures.
cues.zh: 这让它能充当一个依赖温度的切断开关。多亏了外层弹簧，它始终与锅底紧密贴合，从而确保它与锅的温度基本一致。

cues.en: So long as there's liquid water sitting in that pot, the pot itself cannot get hotter than water's boiling point. This means that the button remains magnetic,
cues.zh: 只要锅里还有液态水，锅本身的温度就不会超过水的沸点。这意味着按钮会保持磁性，

cues.en: and the magnet is able to overcome the force of the inner spring, so the device stays in cook mode. But once the rice has absorbed all the water
cues.zh: 磁铁也能克服内层弹簧的拉力，让设备保持在煮饭模式。但一旦米饭吸收了所有的水，

cues.en: the energy being added to the pot by the heating element is no longer being absorbed as latent heat.
cues.zh: 发热盘施加给锅的能量就不再作为潜热被吸收了。

cues.en: Now, the pot can quickly start to exceed the boiling point of water. And once it gets past the curie point of that little sensing button, the magnet is no longer attracted to it, so the spring overcomes the magnet and the rice cooker switches back to the warming mode. Now I don't know about you, but I think this is some of the most amazing ingenuity out there. This incredibly basic device is not only exploiting the physical properties of water, but also the physical properties of magnetism to automate the cooking of rice in an elegant and effective way.
cues.zh: 此时，锅温会迅速超过水的沸点。一旦超过那个感温小按钮的居里点，磁铁就不再被吸引，弹簧便会弹开磁铁，电饭煲随之切回保温模式。不知道大家怎么看，我觉得这种构思简直巧夺天工。这个极其简陋的装置，不仅利用了水的物理特性，还利用了磁学特性，以一种既优雅又高效的方式实现了自动煮饭。

cues.en: Sure, my fancier rice cooker may have some fuzzy logic and a microcontroller in there, but anybody can program an Arduino with some inputs and outputs.
cues.zh: 当然，我那个更高档的电饭煲可能带点模糊逻辑和微控制器，但随便谁都能给带几个输入输出的 Arduino 写程序。

cues.en: So this is much more interesting, at least I think so. These days only the most basic rice cookers continue to use this method of automation.
cues.zh: 所以这种机制有趣得多，至少我觉得是这样。如今只有最基础的电饭煲还在沿用这种自动化方式。

cues.en: But for decades, this is just how rice cookers worked. I've tried to find when exactly this method was first put into production, and short of looking through every single rice cooker related patent out there, the answer isn't obvious. However, it's been in use at least since the late seventies, having come across this patent. And you might be surprised to learn that rice cookers are a rather recent invention.
cues.zh: 但在过去的几十年里，电饭煲一直就是这样工作的。我曾试图查出这种方法究竟是何时首次投入生产的，除非翻遍所有与电饭煲相关的专利，否则很难找到明确答案。不过从我看到的这项专利来看，它至少在七十年代末就已经在用了。你可能会惊讶地发现，电饭煲其实是个相当现代的发明。

cues.en: When you consider that we've had mechanical refrigeration for over a century now,
cues.zh: 考虑到机械制冷技术已经存在了一个多世纪，

cues.en: it can seem a little weird that it took until 1956
cues.zh: 直到 1956 年才出现，

cues.en: for the first automated rice cooker to appear on sale in Japan, produced by Toshiba.
cues.zh: 由 Toshiba 在日本发售第一款自动电饭煲，这听起来确实有点不可思议。

cues.en: Those early rice cookers used a sort of double boiler to indirectly heat the pot. Everyone's favorite source of knowledge claims that that went out of style in the nineteen sixties, but citation needed. Anyway,
cues.zh: 那些早期的电饭煲采用类似双层蒸锅的结构来间接加热内胆。大家最喜欢的知识百科声称这种设计在六十年代就过时了，但“尚缺引证”。不管怎样，

cues.en: that's it. I hope you enjoyed this video. While I wouldn't necessarily call this device automatic beyond belief,
cues.zh: 内容就是这些。希望大家喜欢这个视频。虽然我未必会把这个装置称为不可思议的自动化，

cues.en: it is certainly among the most clever forms of automation out there. Even if I have to push the lever down. And of course, thanks to everyone supporting the channel on Patreon, with a special thanks going to these nifty people scrolling up your screen. CED part five is coming soon so be on the lookout for it. For now though,
cues.zh: 但这绝对称得上是最巧妙的自动化形式之一。哪怕我还得手动按下杠杆。当然，感谢所有在 Patreon 上支持本频道的朋友，特别感谢屏幕上滚动出现的这些优秀赞助者。CED 第五集很快就来，敬请期待。至于现在，

cues.en: eat up.
cues.zh: 开吃吧。

cues.en: I don't know about you, but I find
cues.zh: 不知道你们怎么想，但我总觉得

cues.zh: 刚发现了个错误。我们尽量修一下。能被永磁体吸引的材料会重新获得
